keepouts.note: The plugged-in Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W (51 x 21 mm), centred on the J14/J15 socket rows. No front post may sit here.

notes: noknok PicoHub MOD-0011 rev 1.0. Derived from hardware/kicad/MOD-0011.kicad_pcb on 2026-10-29. Edge.Cuts = 80 x 40 rectangle (120,80)-(200,120). Payload side = KiCad TOP (all parts and the Pico on F), so coordinates are the KiCad top view with Y flipped up: x = kx - 120, y = 120 - ky. Mounting: the profile uses the 8 edge holes (H5, H6, J8 SWD keyed hole, mezzanine cluster holes J9-J13). The 4 holes H1-H4 around (20,20) sit UNDER the Pico, so no post can reach them; they are left out. Connectors: J1 USB-C power in (PD sink, up to 20 V) opens S, J2 USB-C host port opens N, both at x 68; JST-SH J3/J4 (bus A) open N, J5/J6 (bus B) open S (SM04B-SRSS-TB horizontal: signal pads at local y=-2, mouth at +y). The Pico's own micro-USB is deliberately not given an opening. Heights: clearance_top 15.0 = 8.5 female socket + ~2.5 Pico male-header spacer + 1.0 Pico PCB + ~3.0 Pico top parts, PROVISIONAL until calipered on an assembled board; clearance_bottom 3.5 = socket THT pin tails (~3 mm) + margin. The JST and USB-C sockets are on the top side, so the configurator adds no support columns under them. Vent: grille 17 x 7 of dia 3.0 at 4.5 mm (~35% open) over the whole board, so the TPS54302 buck (U2), its inductor (L1), the AP2114H LDOs (U6/U9) and the Pico all vent upward; assumption: convection through the top grille is enough for normal loads in PLA (DEV-146 open). If a print runs hot, next steps in order: bigger vent holes, a larger surrounding box, PETG. Kept reachable: J8 SWD pads and the mezzanine pads are on the bottom, exposed when the bottom cover is off. A fitted mezzanine is not supported by this profile. Housing generated by the Ecosystem housing-configurator (module 'PicoHub'); NOT yet print-validated (verified=false).
